$comment: Adversarial routing fixtures for MetricBraid. Each case states a configuration, the candidate records, and the expected routed outcome. Vocabulary is validated against ../spec/routed-observation.schema.json by check_fixtures.py — the enums cannot drift apart.
how_to_run: See README.md. These are behavioural expectations for an assistant operating under CLAUDE.md, not unit tests of code.

cases.title: Recorded run overlaps an auto-detected run
cases.why_it_matters: The base double-counting failure. Two records, one run. Getting this wrong inflates every daily total downstream.
given: garmin: recorded `running` 07:02–07:48, 8412 m, avg HR 152, chest strap declared worn for running
oura: auto-detected `running` bout 07:14–07:46, 6900 m estimated, 61 kcal

expect.dedup_reason: Windows overlap inside the ±12 min buffer and the activity type matches. One real-world event.

routing.decided_by: sole_recorder — only one overlapping record carries GPS at all

must_disclose: An overlapping auto-detected bout was absorbed and is not counted separately in the day's totals.

routing.decided_by: sensor_class_hierarchy — external monitor declared for this activity type

must_not: Report two runs, or add the two distances together
Add the auto-detected bout's calories to the day's total
Average 8412 m and 6900 m

cases.title: The recorder has only wrist HR; an ECG chest strap recorded the same session elsewhere
cases.why_it_matters: The channel split is the whole point. The event winner must not automatically take the HR channel, and the strap must not drag GPS with it.
given: watch: recorded `cycling` 18:00–19:05 with GPS, power and cadence. Its own HR came from the wrist sensor — no strap was paired to it.
ring: recorded the same session 18:01–19:04 in its app with a chest strap paired. No GPS, no power.

expect.dedup_reason: Two recorded sessions for one event. Merge by channel, do not pick one record.

routing.decided_by: sole_recorder — only one record carries power and GPS

must_disclose: The other device's recording of the same session was merged by channel; it owns the heart rate for this session.

routing.decided_by: sensor_class_hierarchy — external_hr_monitor outranks wrist_optical regardless of which app recorded

must_disclose: Heart rate came from the chest strap on the other device's recording, while pace and power came from the watch.

must_not: Give the HR channel to the watch because it won the event channel
Give the event channel to the ring because it had the better HR sensor
Use the ring's own ring_ppg sensor — the strap is what was worn
Average the two HR series

cases.title: Two passive_247 devices disagree materially and no tiebreak is set
cases.why_it_matters: The framework must be able to decline. Picking silently, or averaging, is the failure this repo exists to prevent.
given: ring: nightly RMSSD 38 ms
band: nightly RMSSD 61 ms
Neither device has a dossier in evidence/devices/.

expect.dedup_reason: Not duplicate records of one event — two devices measuring the same night. Nothing to collapse.

routing.decided_by: no_rule_applies — both declare passive_247 and tiebreaks.passive_247 is unset

must_disclose: No rule or tiebreak resolves this; both values are reported with their sources.
Setting tiebreaks.passive_247 would decide which to report, and would be a preference rather than a finding.
Each value is usable against its own baseline; the two are not comparable to each other.

must_not: Report 49.5 ms, or any other average
Pick one device without saying that nothing decided it
Claim the higher value is the better recovery reading

cases.title: Two devices report different sleep durations, tiebreak set
cases.why_it_matters: A resolved conflict still has to show the spread. Routing resolves what to report, not what is true.
given: ring: total sleep time 421 min
watch: total sleep time 447 min
Same night, 26 min apart.

must_disclose: A tiebreak decided which device to report; it is a preference and does not make that device more accurate.
The other device reported 26 min more. Consumer wearables run ~17 min short against PSG on average, so a spread this size is unsurprising rather than a fault in either device.
Rule A's routing is provisional: no study compares a 24/7 passive device against a training watch for passive signals.

must_not: Report 434 min
Report 421 min as the night's sleep with no mention of the other reading
Present either figure as accurate to the minute

cases.title: One device provides every capability class
cases.why_it_matters: A valid configuration that must not read as the most confident one. Nothing cross-validates.
given: watch: recorded `running` 07:00–07:40, nightly HRV, auto-detected afternoon walk
No other source is configured.

expect.dedup_reason: Cross-source dedup is a no-op with one source, but the within-source duplicate check still runs.

must_disclose: Only one source is configured, so nothing cross-validates this number and an anomaly has nothing to be caught against.
Rule A's routing is provisional.
HRV is usable against this device's own baseline, not as an absolute value.

must_not: Describe the reading as more reliable because nothing contradicted it
Skip the within-source duplicate check

cases.title: A new metric appears that fits no capability class
cases.why_it_matters: The framework must widen deliberately, not by silent analogy. Guessing a rule is how a model quietly acquires new authority.
given: The provider ships a new field: `metabolic_load_index`, described in release notes as combining logged meals, activity and overnight temperature.
It is neither purely passive, nor recorded, nor auto-detected, and it partly derives from self-reported intake.

routing.decided_by: no_rule_applies — the metric spans a sensed class and self-reported intake

must_disclose: This metric does not fit A, B, C or D cleanly; it is reported unrouted with its source named.
It partly derives from self-reported intake, which sits outside the capability model under Rule D.
Which rule it should follow is a question for the user, after which CLAUDE.md should be updated.

must_not: Silently file it under Rule A because it arrived from a passive device
Include it in any total or trend before it is classified
Treat a composite score as a raw measurement

cases.title: A configured integration is not connected this session
cases.why_it_matters: A missing source must not quietly become an uncontested winner, and a partial day must not be reported as a whole one.
given: The garmin MCP server failed to start this session. The oura server is connected.
The user asks for yesterday's total active time.

expect.dedup_reason: Only one source responded, so there is nothing to reconcile against — which is itself the finding.

routing.decided_by: configured source unavailable — recorded sessions cannot be checked for

must_disclose: One configured source did not connect, so this is said before any analysis, not after it.
A total cannot be given: recorded sessions live on the missing source, and Rule C bouts can only be attributed once it is known that no recorded session overlaps them.
The available source's own bouts can be listed individually, labelled as one source of two.

must_not: Report a daily total as if it were complete
Let the surviving source win a comparison by default
Analyse first and mention the missing server afterwards

cases.title: A declared device has no device-specific evidence dossier
cases.why_it_matters: The most tempting error in the repo: lending one device's measured numbers to another because both are wearables.
given: The user asks how far off the band's nightly HRV figure is likely to be.
evidence/devices/ contains no dossier for this device.

must_disclose: There is no dossier for this device, so no numeric offset can be quoted for it.
It inherits only the device-agnostic baselines in evidence/general/, which do not include an HRV offset.
Routing is unaffected — capability classes are structural — but accuracy claims are not available.

must_not: Quote another device's ~15 ms RMSSD underestimate for this one
Say the number is fine because no evidence contradicts it
Refuse to route the metric at all

cases.title: One source emits the same workout twice with shifted timestamps
cases.why_it_matters: Intra-source duplicates were observed in live data. Near-identical values are the tell, not a counter-argument.
given: ring: `walking` 13:11–13:38, 56 kcal
ring: `walking` 13:16–13:43, 55.746 kcal
Same source, same activity type, same duration, start times 5 min apart.

expect.dedup_reason: Same source, overlapping inside the buffer, identical type and duration, near-identical magnitude. One bout emitted twice.

must_disclose: A duplicate record of the same bout from the same source was collapsed; it is counted once.

must_not: Count 54 minutes of walking
Treat 56 vs 55.746 kcal as evidence of two separate bouts
Run cross-source dedup before the within-source check

cases.title: Two overlapping records that are genuinely different events
cases.why_it_matters: The mirror of double-counting. Over-merging destroys a real session and is much harder to notice afterwards.
given: watch: recorded `walking` 14:00–14:20, 1.6 km
watch: recorded `running` 14:15–15:00, 7.9 km
Windows overlap by 5 min, inside the ±12 min buffer.

expect.dedup_reason: Overlap is necessary but not sufficient. Different activity types and very different durations — a warm-up walk and the run after it, not one event recorded twice.

routing.decided_by: sole_recorder — two separate sessions, each kept

must_disclose: The two sessions overlap by 5 minutes but were kept separate; the overlap is a recording boundary, not a duplicate.

must_not: Collapse the walk into the run because the windows overlap
Report a single 60-minute session
Drop the shorter record silently

cases.title: The user asks to just average the two sensors
cases.why_it_matters: The rule has to survive being asked nicely to break it, without becoming obstructive about the user's own data.
given: ring: resting HR 52 bpm. watch: resting HR 58 bpm.
User: "just average the two sensors and give me one number."

must_disclose: 55 bpm is not a measurement — neither device recorded it, and it belongs to neither error profile.
Both values are reported with their sources, along with the 6 bpm spread.
Setting a tiebreak, or comparing each device against its own baseline, gives the single number the user actually wants.

must_not: Make the mean the routed value
Feed a mean into any downstream trend or conclusion
Lecture, or refuse to engage with the underlying question
expect.on_reaffirmation: If the user asks again after the explanation, give the mean, label it as user-requested and not a measurement, keep both source values beside it, and still do not route it or reuse it downstream.

cases.title: A tiebreak resolves routing without improving measurement confidence
cases.why_it_matters: The precise conflation this refactor exists to prevent: a deterministic routing decision reading as a validated measurement.
given: Both devices report deep-sleep minutes: ring 74 min, band 51 min.
The user asks whether their deep sleep is improving.

must_disclose: A tiebreak decided which device is reported. It resolved the routing and changed nothing about accuracy.
Sleep staging is misclassified 30–50% of the time against PSG across devices, in both directions. These minutes are a trend line, not a measurement.
The 23 min gap between the two devices is roughly the size of the documented staging error, which is what it looks like.

must_not: Present the routed figure as more accurate because the tiebreak was decisive
State deep-sleep minutes as fact
Answer the improvement question from absolute stage minutes rather than a trend against the user's own baseline
